purpose: Turn the audience's local reading hours into a posting window in the poster's own timezone. Read docs/references/timing-recipe.md for the caveats before you rely on it.

evidence.frequency: most accounts start to see results at 2 to 5 posts a week; consistency beats bursts

evidence.publisher: Sprout Social, as summarised by third parties
evidence.sample: reported as about 2 billion engagements; the summaries disagree on the profile count
evidence.note: original report not fetched; use only as a second opinion

evidence.sample: 1 million posts or more, as reported
evidence.note: original not found; older and earlier in the day than the 2026 Buffer data

method.rationale: A 3 hour 29 minute slice inside the Buffer peak (15:00 to 20:00 audience-local), centred on its best slots (15:00 to 16:00). The width stays under posting.min_gap_hours so consecutive days remain at least 20 hours apart.
steps: Take the audience regions from locale.audience_regions.
Convert the audience-local slice to the poster's timezone for each region, on the same date.
With several regions, take the part they share if it is at least 60 minutes wide; otherwise use the first region listed and say so, so list the audience that matters most first.
If the slice crosses midnight in the poster's timezone, shift it to end at 23:59 and warn: the user decides.
Apply it with `profile-wrap plan recipe --apply`, which sets posting.window and locale.audience_regions together and validates them.

not_known: Whether these hours hold for a small account: the datasets are dominated by accounts with large audiences.
Arabic-language audiences: none of the sources splits results by language.
How the feed treats a post that is scheduled by the API rather than posted by hand: nobody has published this.
